title: A political right cannot be used twice
text: Once a citizen is eligible to participate, the system still needs one more guarantee: that the same political right cannot be exercised twice. That is where the nullifier appears.
visualHint: Electoral panel marking a single valid participation per citizen

title: A nullifier marks usage without revealing identity
text: A nullifier is a unique usage mark. It lets the contract know that participation already happened without exposing which citizen performed it.
visualHint: 'Right already exercised' stamp applied without showing identity

title: How a nullifier is generated
text: The book shows the formula: nullifier = hash(secret_key + event). This way, each pair (user, action) produces a unique value but is not reversible to discover the identity.
visualHint: Hash function taking two inputs and producing a unique code

title: The nullifier lives in the ledger
text: Once generated, the nullifier is published to the ledger. The smart contract stores it so that the next time the same citizen tries to participate, the system detects the repetition and rejects the action.

title: The double-voting problem
text: Without nullifiers, a malicious citizen could try to vote multiple times. In a private voting system, the threat is real: detect repetition without turning the election into a database of exposed identities.
visualHint: Duplicate ballots blocked by a verification shield

title: The exclusion mark resolves the conflict
text: Each time voting rights are exercised, the system records a nullifier. The next attempt finds that same mark and gets rejected automatically.
visualHint: Electoral console showing an already registered nullifier

title: Double-spending: the same problem
text: The book extends the concept to tokens: if someone tries to spend the same token twice, the second attempt fails because the first transaction already consumed (nullified) that token's commitment.
visualHint: Coin split into two copies, one accepted and one rejected

title: Privacy is maintained
text: The trick is that the ledger only sees the nullifier, not the identity. The contract only knows that 'something has been spent' but cannot link it to a specific user identity.
visualHint: Encryption protecting identity while showing 'used' status

title: Linkability: relating without revealing
text: Sometimes you want to link two actions from the same user without revealing who they are. For example: verifying someone is eligible for multiple airdrop rounds without exposing their identity.
visualHint: Chain of events linked by a hidden identifier

title: The nonce enables multiple linked actions
text: The book introduces the nonce as a counter that increments with each action. Combined with the user's secret key, it produces different nullifiers for each action while still being linkable to each other.
visualHint: Counter generating different codes for each use

title: Formula with nonce
text: The book's formula is: nullifier = hash(secret_key + nonce). If nonce is 0, 1, 2..., each action produces a unique nullifier and the contract can verify that all come from the same user.
visualHint: Hash equation with nonce producing multiple outputs

title: Granular control of linking
text: By choosing what data to include in the hash, the system controls when there is linkability and when there isn't. If you want completely independent actions, you just use the secret key without a nonce.
visualHint: Control panel with switches to activate/deactivate linking

title: Application: private voting system
text: The book shows a real case: each voter generates a nullifier with their secret key. The contract saves it in a set of already-used nullifiers. The election result is public, but who voted for whom remains private.
visualHint: Electronic ballot box with exclusion witness

title: Application: airdrop distribution
text: For an airdrop, the contract can verify eligibility through ZK proofs, and each eligible address generates a nullifier when claiming their tokens. That prevents claiming twice.
visualHint: Token distribution box with single-use verification

title: The circuit validates the nullifier
text: The contract uses a circuit to verify two things: (1) the nullifier was correctly generated using the user's secret key, and (2) it doesn't already exist in the ledger's nullifier set.
visualHint: Circuit validating a nullifier before storing it

title: The nullifier set is the key
text: The book concludes: without a public nullifier set, there's no way to prevent double-spending or double-voting. The set is your exclusion list, and each new nullifier must be checked against it before accepting the action.
visualHint: Growing list of unique codes with verification on each new entry
